spec.reason: The renderer cannot draw a map from a spec it cannot read.

spec-unknown-key.message: Unknown field {path}. It is ignored. Fields allowed here: {allowed}.
spec-unknown-key.reason: A misspelled field is ignored without a word, so the map would not do what you meant.

source-required.message: The map has no source line.
source-required.reason: Readers cannot check a map that does not say where the numbers come from. Add "source" to the spec.

title-required.reason: Readers should know what the colours measure before they read the legend.

legend-title.message: The legend has no title, so the unit of {column} is not stated.
legend-title.reason: A number without a unit can be read several ways. Set data.label, for example "Deaths per 100,000 people".

kind-undeclared.message: data.kind is not set, so raw counts cannot be ruled out.
kind-undeclared.reason: Shading raw counts mostly shows where many people live. Declare "kind" as rate, share, index or count.

value-not-numeric.message: Column {column} is mostly not numeric (for example "{example}").
value-not-numeric.reason: Only numbers can be sorted into the classes of a legend.

no-values.message: No area has a numeric value to draw.

join-failed.message: Only {percent}% of the rows in column {column} matched an area of {region} as {kind}. Not matched: {examples}.
join-failed.reason: A map built on a failed join puts values in the wrong places. Check data.key, data.keyType and region.

join-unmatched.message: {count} rows matched no area and are not drawn: {list}.
join-unmatched.message_one: {count} row matched no area and is not drawn: {list}.
join-unmatched.reason: Rows that vanish quietly make a map look complete when it is not. Fix the spelling or the key column.

join-ambiguous.message: These names fit more than one area, so they are not drawn: {list}.
join-ambiguous.reason: Guessing which area was meant would put a value in the wrong place.

duplicate-keys.message: {count} areas have more than one row (for example {example} has {rows}).
duplicate-keys.message_one: {count} area has more than one row (for example {example} has {rows}).
duplicate-keys.reason: Only one value can be drawn per area, and keeping the last row hides the others. Set data.aggregate, or data.filter to pick one row such as one year.

raw-counts.message_declared: The values are raw counts (data.kind is count).
raw-counts.message_correlated: The values track population (Spearman correlation {rho} with the population of each area), which is what raw counts do.
raw-counts.reason: A map of counts mostly shows where people live. Divide by population or area so that the colours show a rate. --fix does it when the region has population data.

projection-mercator.message: Mercator on a region {span} degrees of latitude tall.
projection-mercator.reason: Mercator stretches area away from the equator, so Greenland looks as large as Africa, and a choropleth is compared by area. Use an equal-area projection.

projection-not-equal-area.reason: Areas read larger or smaller than they are, which biases the comparison a little. Equal Earth, Albers and Lambert azimuthal keep areas true.

max-classes.message: {count} classes is more than readers can tell apart. The limit is {max}.
max-classes.reason: People can match about seven shades against a legend and no more.

class-breaks-coverage.message: The class edges run from {low} to {high} but the data runs from {min} to {max}.
class-breaks-coverage.reason: A value outside the first and last edge gets no colour, so the legend would not describe the map. List every edge, lowest value first and highest last.

empty-class.reason: A legend entry that nothing uses suggests the breaks do not fit the data.

skewed-classes.message: {percent}% of the areas fall into one class.
skewed-classes.reason: Equal intervals and hand-set breaks on skewed data paint most of the map one colour. Quantile or Jenks classes spread the areas out.

palette-order.message: Palette {palette} does not get steadily lighter or darker.
palette-order.reason: On a sequential scale the order of lightness is the only sign of "more". Rainbow palettes jump up and down in lightness and invent boundaries.

cvd-separation.message: Colours of palette {palette} come as close as a CIEDE2000 difference of {worst} for some viewers with colour vision deficiency.
cvd-separation.reason: About 1 in 12 men cannot tell some of these colours apart. Neighbouring classes need a difference of at least 3, and 5 is comfortable (8 for categories).

diverging-center.message: Diverging palette {palette} needs a centre value.
diverging-center.reason: Without a meaningful midpoint, such as 0, a diverging scale suggests a split that the data does not have. Set "center".

too-many-categories.message: {count} categories is more than the {max} colours a legend can carry.
too-many-categories.reason: Beyond eight colours readers cannot match the map to the legend. Group the small categories as Other.

no-data-share.reason: A map with large grey areas can mislead. Say why in the note, or pick a region that the data covers.

label-overlap.reason: Labels that overlap cannot be read.

highlight-unmatched.message: Could not find these highlight areas: {list}.
highlight-unmatched.reason: A locator map that highlights nothing shows nothing.

symbols-negative.message: Proportional symbols cannot show {count} values at or below zero.
symbols-negative.message_one: Proportional symbols cannot show {count} value at or below zero.
symbols-negative.reason: The area of a circle stands for a quantity, so a negative value has no size.

fix-applied.reason: --fix makes the smallest change that satisfies the rule and lists it here.

labels-hidden.message: {count} labels were left out because they do not fit inside their area or would overlap another label.
labels-hidden.message_one: {count} label was left out because it does not fit inside its area or would overlap another label.
labels-hidden.reason: Hidden labels are listed so that a quieter map is not mistaken for a complete one.

small-areas-marked.message: {count} areas are too small to see at this scale and are drawn as dots.
small-areas-marked.message_one: {count} area is too small to see at this scale and is drawn as a dot.
small-areas-marked.reason: Small countries and territories would otherwise vanish from the map.

outside-frame.message: {count} areas with data lie outside the map frame: {list}.
outside-frame.message_one: {count} area with data lies outside the map frame: {list}.
outside-frame.reason: They are not drawn. Pick a larger region to show them.

normalize-missing.message: {count} areas have no bundled {by} to divide by and are shown as no data.
normalize-missing.message_one: {count} area has no bundled {by} to divide by and is shown as no data.
normalize-missing.reason: A rate cannot be computed without a denominator. Supply one with normalize.by column, or accept the gaps and say so in the note.

values-skipped.message: {count} rows reached an area but were left out because a cell is not a number, or a value has a missing or zero denominator (for example {example}).
values-skipped.message_one: {count} row reached an area but was left out because a cell is not a number, or a value has a missing or zero denominator (for example {example}).
values-skipped.reason: A skipped row changes the value of its area with no sign on the map. Fix the cell, or accept the gap and say so in the note.

table-ragged.message: {count} rows have a different number of cells than the header.
table-ragged.message_one: {count} row has a different number of cells than the header.
table-ragged.reason: Cells in a short or long row may sit under the wrong column. Check the quoting and the delimiter of the file.

table-encoding.message: {file} is not valid UTF-8, so it was read as {encoding}. If names look wrong, set data.encoding (for example big5, shift_jis, euc-kr or gbk) or save the file as UTF-8.
table-encoding.reason: Spreadsheets on Windows often save CSV in the system code page. Read with the wrong one, a name turns into other characters and its row matches no area.

boundaries-skipped.message: {count} features of {file} are not drawn because they have no polygon (a point, a line or no geometry).
boundaries-skipped.message_one: {count} feature of {file} is not drawn because it has no polygon (a point, a line or no geometry).
boundaries-skipped.reason: Only polygons can be shaded. A feature without one cannot show a value, so its row cannot appear on the map.

join-blank.message: {count} rows have an empty name in the key column and are not drawn.
join-blank.message_one: {count} row has an empty name in the key column and is not drawn.
join-blank.reason: A row that names no area cannot be placed. A blank key is often a total row or a note at the end of the table.

glyphs-missing.message: The embedded fonts have no glyph for these characters: {list}.
glyphs-missing.reason: They would show as empty boxes. Use a different spelling or a different label language.

symbols-min-size.message: {count} symbols are smaller than the minimum size and were drawn at the minimum.
symbols-min-size.message_one: {count} symbol is smaller than the minimum size and was drawn at the minimum.
symbols-min-size.reason: Those circles are slightly larger than their value says. They are listed so that sizes are not read too precisely.

data.encodingNote: This file is not UTF-8, so it was read as {encoding}. If the names look wrong, pick the right encoding.
data.boundaries: {count} areas read from {file}. Add a table that names them.
data.boundaries_one: {count} area read from {file}. Add a table that names it.
data.dropHint: A CSV is the table. A GeoJSON or TopoJSON file adds your own boundaries.
data.empty: Add a table and the map appears here.

map.highlight: Areas to highlight (names or codes, separated by commas)

export.hint: Every file is made in your browser.

stage.blocked: Fix the errors on the left to see the map.

footer.note: Open source, MIT license. Everything runs in your browser and nothing is uploaded.
